transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Alex from Redwood, AE on this account. Quick intro, Priya and Samir are with me from our SE team.
[00:06] Dana Morris: Hi Alex, hi team, Dana here. Thanks for setting this up.
[00:10] Luis Ortega: Luis on the call; we're the ML engs, curious about time-to-first-token and cost per inference.
[00:15] Priya Rao: Great, thanks. The goal today is a quick discovery - where you're at, goals, and whether you want self-serve hosted API or something more isolated like Dedicated or Private.
[00:25] Dana: High-level, Aperture builds analytics features inside our product - summarization, entity extraction, and assistant workflows. We're looking to add LLM features quickly, ideally PLG/self-serve first, but we have enterprise customers that may push for VPC or on-prem later.
[00:40] Tom Liu: From infra, we care about SLA, region control, and KMS integration - can't have keys leaving our account for certain customers.
[00:48] Alex: Totally. Redwood supports hosted API for fast onboarding with free credits and quickstart SDKs. Dedicated for predictable throughput and isolation. Private if you need a VPC or on-prem package with KMS/HSM.
[01:00] Luis: For hosted, how quick is time-to-first-token? We want devs to try within an hour.
[01:06] Priya: Typical time-to-first-token for the quickstart is under 15 minutes: sign up, apply credits, API key, and run sample curl or Python SDK. We'll share snippets. In practice, first API call latency depends on model and seq length - 20-200ms per token for our curated small-medium models on hosted.
[01:25] Samir: Also streaming is supported for chat responses, and we have sample apps to show immediate integration.
[01:32] Dana: Ok. Our main metric is 95th percentile latency under 500ms for conversational features, and cost per 1k tokens needs to be competitive vs our alternatives.
[01:42] Alex: Understood. For throughput, Dedicated helps with SLOs; for cost we often recommend quantized model variants or caching prefixes. Redwood Optimize gives batching/caching suggestions.
[01:55] Luis: Do you have benchmarks for common models? We use a mix of open models and some proprietary fine-tunes.
[02:02] Priya: We maintain a model catalog with verified perf profiles. I'll send the benchmark checklist and a sample spreadsheet showing latency/cost tradeoffs across model families and instance types - it's useful for selecting hosted vs dedicated.
[02:15] Meera Shah: Security questions - SOC 2, data retention, audit logs, SSO. Also KMS: if we go Dedicated, can we bring our own KMS?
[02:26] Alex: Yes, Dedicated and Private support customer-managed KMS integrations and audit logs. Hosted is encrypted at rest with Redwood keys, but we offer contracts for higher tiers. We can share our security pack - SOC 2 and ISO artifacts are available under NDA.
[02:40] Meera: Great. Also need to know about data traces: are prompts stored for model improvements?
[02:45] Priya: By default hosted may use telemetry to improve models unless opted-out; for enterprise customers we offer opt-out and controls. Private/Dedicated can be configured to keep data in-customer scope. We'll include exact retention options in the security doc.
[02:58] Tom: Network-wise, if Dedicated sits in our cloud, can we restrict egress to our VPC?
[03:04] Samir: With Private/VPC you control networking. Dedicated offers isolated GPU pools and can be deployed in selected regions; there's also private control plane options for stricter isolation. We'll map the exact networking patterns in the technical deep dive.
[03:20] Dana: Budget/timeline - we want to pilot in the next 4 weeks, evaluating hosted quickstart first, then a small Dedicated POC if numbers look good. Does Redwood provide free credits for pilots?
[03:30] Alex: Yes, we provide trial credits for onboarding plus a quickstart checklist. For pilots that move to Dedicated, we can discuss committed usage discounts.
[03:38] Luis: One more on latency - for our summarization use case we do shorter prompts but need low tail latency. What are typical tradeoffs?
[03:44] Priya: Tail latency often comes from cold-starts and batching. We recommend prefix caching for repeated system prompts, and continuous warm workers for Dedicated to minimize cold-starts. For hosted, we can configure warm pools at higher tiers.
[03:58] Dana: Any restrictions on fine-tuning or adapters? We plan a light re-tune for domain style.
[04:03] Alex: Hosted supports instruction tuning and lightweight fine-tunes for some models; Dedicated/Private allow more flexibility and local model variants. We'll share the model onboarding docs.
[04:15] Luis: How about SDKs - we want a node + python quickstart.
[04:19] Priya: We have SDKs and examples: node, python, curl, and a React sample for streaming chat. Time-to-first-token is usually driven by key issuance and running the sample call. I'll attach snippets.
[04:31] Dana: Great. Who will be our day-to-day contact if we spin up a pilot?
[04:35] Alex: I'll be the account AE, Priya and Samir will support technical onboarding. For pilots we usually assign a CSM once committed.
[04:41] Meera: Compliance-wise, please email our security questionnaire. We need to hit SOC 2 and have RBAC & SAML.
[04:48] Alex: Will do. I'll send the security pack and a prioritized answers doc.
[04:52] Tom: One more question: competitor lock-in - if we start on hosted and later want Private, how easy is migration?
[04:58] Samir: We expose the same API and model versioning across deployment modes, so code changes are minimal. Model artifacts and prompts can be ported; we'll map any infra-specific steps in the migration plan.
[05:12] Luis: Billing model - is it pure usage-based? Any reservations?
[05:16] Alex: Hosted is usage-based. Dedicated is reserve/pool contracts for steady throughput. Private has licensing plus infra. We can show sample cost models tailored to your expected token volumes.
[05:28] Dana: Success criteria for us: 1) devs can integrate via SDKs within a day, 2) POC demonstrates 95th pctl latency <500ms for 80% of calls, 3) cost per 1M tokens within X (we'll share target number).
[05:45] Priya: Good. We'll support with quickstart, bench checklist, and a pilot plan.
[05:52] Alex: Recap / next steps: I'll send pricing, trial credit details, and the security pack. Priya will send the benchmark checklist and quickstart snippets. We'll schedule a deeper infra call week of 2026-09-13 to discuss Dedicated/Private network/KMS. Luis, you'll share the sample prompt set and current usage.
[06:10] Dana: Sounds good. Any immediate blockers?
[06:13] Meera: None besides the security questionnaire.
[06:16] Alex: Great. Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the artifacts.
[06:20] Luis: Thanks. Bye.

Note: transcription contains occasional misheard words; proper nouns (e.g., model family names) may be slightly off. Sample artifacts referenced: security_pack_link (redwood.com/security/pack), quickstart_snippets (redwood.com/quickstart), benchmark_sheet (redwood.com/benchmarks/apt), pricing_estimate_draft (link to be sent).
